fields.summary: محلہ الکوت کے قلب میں تقریباً تین صدیاں پرانی ایک مسجد، جو الاحساء کے ورثے کا حصہ ہے۔ یہ الملا خاندان سے وابستہ رہی ہے، جو ایک علمی گھرانہ ہے۔
fields.body: مسجد شیخ محمد بن ابی بکر الملا، ہفوف کے تاریخی محلہ الکوت کے قلب میں، شیخ ابو بکر کے گھر اور ان کے دینی مدارس کے قریب واقع ہے۔ اسے مشرقی مسجد بھی کہتے ہیں۔ یہ الاحساء کے ورثے کی قدیم ترین مساجد میں سے ایک ہے، اور تقریباً تین صدیاں پرانی ہے۔ یہ مٹی، بجری اور کھجور کے تنوں سے بنی ہے۔ طویل عرصے تک یہ علم کا مرکز رہی، جہاں فقہ، تفسیر اور نحو کے درس ہوتے تھے، اور اس کے امام نسل در نسل الملا خاندان سے ہوتے رہے، جو ایک علمی گھرانہ ہے۔ “شہزادہ محمد بن سلمان منصوبے” کے پہلے مرحلے میں اس کی بحالی ہوئی۔ یہ تاریخی مساجد کے لیے ایک ترقیاتی منصوبہ ہے، اور اس کا پہلا مرحلہ 1441 ہجری (2020 عیسوی) میں مکمل ہوا۔ بحالی میں مسجد کی روایتی وضع برقرار رکھی گئی، اور اس میں تقریباً 125 نمازیوں کی گنجائش ہے۔

blind_reader_rulings.reason: Three things in one remark. That four of the five cards give no hours and no page gives a way to reach anyone is the source's (no Hours row, no operator link), logged with the owner's pending question. The two sentences are approved text reused verbatim: ruling N16, point 3 a — the short name as the press writes it, inflected, inside quotation marks, and what the programme is for in a clause of its own. A ruling is not reopened and a pair of the translation memory is not broken. Recorded for the owner, now on both readers of the batch and charged under nativeness on three pages: the name seems bent by grammar because the inflected noun stands inside the marks; one learns only from the flat second sentence what the project is for; its adjective is office Urdu that suggests roads and drains; his own wording puts the full description before the name. His part (d), that the summary of umzurainiq and the page of the port name the scheme otherwise so that he cannot tell whether these are one project or three, is the source's (three names in the sources), logged.

Words and figures are each as the English field has them, and 'about' stands where the source puts it, before exact figures too; nothing is converted or evened out (ruling N12). Logged; both readers noticed.

'One of the oldest' stands in the sources of hubaish and abubakr-mosque for ages centuries apart, each under its 'one of'; the Urdu neither adds nor drops a superlative (ruling P19). He quotes round 1's verb for the century of hubaish and has no remark on it. Logged: read together, the claim stops meaning anything to both readers.

The title is the pattern item N43 rules for both tahimiyah pages, and the second name of abubakr-mosque is its source's own, translated by the English. Two mosques in two places carry one describing name in both sources; nothing in the Urdu can tell them apart without adding to one of them. Two readers of two: the stated cost of N43, charged under fit on tahimiyah-e.
No page of the source says anything of a place for women to pray, of ablution or of parking. Nothing is supplied. Logged for the owner in his words: 'it is what decides whether we stop'.

The value is item N41's, word for word. Logged with the owner's pending question.

Both languages say twice that the mountain is near, and neither says what the mountain is to a visitor or why one would be going there. This is the string round 1 changed (the mountain by its name where stage 5 had 'that mountain'): the first reader had lost the antecedent across the sentence about 2017, and the second does not; what he reports is the source's repetition and the source's silence. The edit stands. His remedy, to drop the first mention, would take a statement of the source out. 'The First Tahimiyah Mosque' is a name in both sources, with no word on whether it was the first built or the first one meets. Nothing is supplied. Logged; both readers asked.

The string round 1 changed. The first reader met two sentences with no link; they are one sentence now, as in the English, and what the second reader still misses is the reason — which the English does not state. The Arabic alone gives the prayers as the reason for the name; that is Arabic-only content and is not imported, and neither language says what the name means. The edit stands; logged.

Both sources say exactly this ('its history goes back centuries'), and that no century is given is theirs. His other point, that «تاریخ … پرانی ہے» is loose, is the second reader's echo of the first (who offered «یہ مسجد صدیوں پرانی ہے»): the collocation stands on the reference site for this very statement, and the offered wording says that the building is centuries old, a little more than the sources say of a mud structure. Kept; two readers of two, charged under nativeness, and the wording stays on record for the owner.

His remedy, a sentence of its own after the list, is the owner's to take.

Whether the direction belongs to the name is the cost of a half-translated name (item N63), which the district word does not cure: the first reader had the same doubt in the body, where it stands.

Ruling N34, not reopened by a batch judge: the arch is the one word, marked on a mosque page by the plural, and no other word is brought in for it. He is the fourth reader of the round to take the plural for prayer niches, and the second on pages that name no niche. Each statement is carried at its strength with the source's figures. Serious for both readers; logged first among the harms of this page.

The source says twice that the mosque is named after the cemetery beside it and never gives the cemetery's name; nothing is supplied. That the first word of the name reads to him as a woman's kunya, and that he cannot say the second, are the name's own letters (ruling P17: no vowel sign), charged under fit.

The source hangs both features on one 'distinguished by'; stage 1 gave the hallmark a sentence of its own, and the particle marks the second as the second. Minor for both readers; a second word for the same statement would be a change for taste. Counted under nativeness.

Whether the mosque is among the closed parts, whether one can go in or pray, and entry to what, are said by neither language; that the body's 'was restored' sits beside works under way in the card is the owner's own arrangement. The cost that ruling states is met again — the two look-alike words side by side, and a word that does not say what the building was. The owner's claim in its one approved wording (build check C34: the first seaport, never the oldest); how the site states a claim of its own is not changed on a reader's remark (rulings P24 and P25). source_defects.where: uqair-mosque: the card, and the card against the body (first reader: observations 34 serious, 35); second reader: items 31 serious, 32
source_defects.defect: By the owner's ruling of 2026-10-02 this mosque's card has no visiting row. Its first row, 'Site status', speaks of the port complex ('undergoing restoration work, and some parts may be closed'); its second says 'Free entry' without saying of what. Neither language says whether the mosque itself is open or among the closed parts, whether one may go in or pray there, whether the compound has hours, or how far the port lies from Hofuf. The body says the mosque 'was restored' while the card says works are under way. ROUND 2: serious again for the second reader, who adds that the page gives no distance or driving time from Hofuf, where the tahimiyah page gives one.
source_defects.effect_on_urdu: Both rows are carried as they stand (item N55) and no visiting row is supplied; the body says nothing of works under way. HARM, the greatest in the batch: this is the farthest of the five places, and the reader 'would not drive a family to the coast on this card'. FOR THE OWNER: one line saying whether the mosque can be entered while the works last. ROUND 2, one thing the Urdu sharpens and the record had not named (the proof pass's finding 6): since round 1 the page calls the mosque one of the port's «حصوں» in summary and body, and the card says that some «حصے» may be closed — one Urdu noun where the English keeps 'facilities' and 'parts' apart. Nothing false is said; both readers asked whether the mosque is among the closed parts, the first before that noun stood in the text.

source_defects.where: umzurainiq: summary and body (first reader: observation 30 serious; 29); second reader: items 27 serious, 28
source_defects.defect: The page calls the mosque 'small' and 'historic', says in the summary that it was 'restored', and then that its rehabilitation expanded it 'from a mere thirty square metres to around 214, with room for some 94 worshippers' — seven times the size, and more worshippers than the 318 square metres of hubaish hold. The English gives no unit after 214; the Arabic says metres without 'square'. Both languages say twice that the mosque is named after the cemetery beside it and never give the cemetery's name. ROUND 2: serious again for the second reader, who doubts that the building he would see is the old one at all.

HARM: the reader no longer knows whether he would see a century-old mosque or a mostly new building, and distrusts the word 'historic'.

source_defects.defect: The body tells the port's story and almost nothing of the mosque: no size, material, look, age, or year of restoration. The summary says the facilities were 'developed under King Abdulaziz' (in the Arabic the King developed them), the body that they were 'built and developed' in his reign, so that the reader cannot tell whether the mosque was built then. calibration.evidence: ROUND 2: the entry is rewritten so that it stands alone and says only what was measured. WHERE IT WAS MET: round 1's text of uqair-mosque::summary carried «جنہیں» once, the first pronoun of the class in any Urdu text of the site; two blind readers read it there and neither remarked on its spelling. WHAT IS SOUND. (1) Press, by script on 2026-10-13 (b4/s7-p22-press.mjs, output s7-p22-press.out.txt): on the three outlets from which article text was fetched — urdunews.com (the Gulf's Urdu paper), express.pk, independenturdu.com — these pronouns are written with a heh and never with U+06BE: 12 and 0, 15 and 0, 18 and 0 tokens; on bbc.com/urdu with U+06BE and never with a heh: 0 and 44. (4) Two blind readers of this batch read «جنہیں» in place without a remark. WHAT WAS NOT SOUND IN ROUND 1's ENTRY AND IS WITHDRAWN FROM THE GROUNDS. (a) It said '12 with U+06C1': the script counts U+06C1 and U+0647 together (some outlets type the Arabic letter), so its counts say 'a heh and not U+06BE', not which heh. The set is in the round's stage checker (see the guard). (e) NEW IN ROUND 2, against the class as round 1 worded it: the same dictionary heads the fifth pronoun of the class with U+06BE (entry page meaning-of-tumhen, title code points 062A 064F 0645 06BE 06CC 06BA; 28 on the page against 3 with U+06C1). calibration.ruling_or_recommendation: RE-WEIGHED IN ROUND 2: THE RULING STANDS, NARROWER. A, for the pronouns a text of this site can carry: «جنہیں», «انہیں», «انہوں», «جنہوں», and the forms built on them, are written with U+06C1. What carries the ruling, and is sound: the three outlets this reader reads that gave article text print them so without exception, the Gulf's Urdu paper among them; the named dictionary heads all three of these words it was read for with U+06C1; two blind readers passed the spelling in place; it is the provisional rule under which every page so far was written, and the spelling the stage checker and role file 05 are built for. B is not an error: it is the spelling of the reference site, of one broadcaster and, as far as is known, of the reformed orthography; it is not written on this site. TAKEN OUT OF THE RULING: the fifth pronoun of round 1's list, «تمہیں», with the other forms of the pronoun «تم». Round 1 ruled it with the class; the one reference read for it heads it with U+06BE, no outlet gave a token of it, and under the site's address rule (config: the honorific pronoun only) no text can carry it. It is not ruled either way; if a quoted text ever needs it, it is raised then with this evidence. Ruling P22a is untouched: U+06BE stays where it is a true aspirate. No approved string changes, because none carries a pronoun of the class, and no string of b4 does since round 2. Limits of the evidence, stated: three outlets against one, on one morning; one of the two named references unread; the committees unread. On record for the owner, one line: if he prefers the reformed spelling, B is a mechanical change over the four forms, none of which stands on the site today.
